title: IDEEL Protocol for DNA Extraction Using Chelex and Tween
author: Infectious Disease Epidemiology and Ecology Lab
materials: Make sure to change tips between each sample.
Change tips when moving to a new row.

steps.title: Prepare Work Area
steps.instruction: Put on gloves and spray the work area with 70% ethanol.

steps.title: Prepare Reagent Dilutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the following dilutions for approximately 200 samples (or 2 x 96-well plates):

substeps.instruction: 1X PBS: Mix 40 ml of 10X PBS with 360 ml of molecular grade water.

0.5% TWEEN® 20 in 1X PBS: Add 9 ml of 1X PBS and 1 ml of 100% TWEEN® 20 into a 50 ml conical tube and vortex, then pour into a 500 ml glass media bottle. Add 190 ml of 1X PBS and shake well. Prepare in advance to allow bubbles to resolve.

10% Chelex: Place 1.5 g of Chelex in a 50 ml conical tube and fill with molecular grade water up to 15 ml. Repeat for a second tube. Vortex sufficiently until the mixture is a homogenous cloudy white liquid.

steps.title: Prepare Punched DBS Plates
steps.instruction: Verify that no Dried Blood Spots (DBS) are stuck to the clear seal of the plates.

substeps.instruction: If DBS are stuck, centrifuge the plate to spin them to the bottom.
If still stuck, gently peel back the seal and use tweezers (cleaned with 70% ethanol and a Chemwipe) to move DBS to the appropriate wells.

steps.title: Initial Incubation with Tween
steps.instruction: Add Tween solution to the DBS and shake overnight.

substeps.instruction: Fill a sterile reservoir with 0.5% TWEEN® 20 in 1X PBS.
Using a P1000 multichannel pipet, add 1 ml of 0.5% TWEEN® 20 in 1X PBS to the wells containing punched DBS.
Ensure DBS are submerged or floating, then seal the plate with a foil seal.
Secure the plate to a shaker and shake overnight at room temperature at 300 rpm.

steps.title: Collect Protein Supernatant
steps.instruction: Recover the supernatant for protein storage if required.

substeps.instruction: Remove plates from shaker and centrifuge briefly at 300 rpm for 1 min (balance the centrifuge if using a single plate).
Match the prepared Protein storage plate label with the extraction plate.
Using a P1000 multichannel pipet, aspirate 300 µL of the supernatant (0.5% TWEEN® 20 in 1X PBS) and transfer to the corresponding wells in the final Protein Plate.
Seal the final protein plate with a foil seal.

steps.title: Wash DBS Samples
steps.instruction: Remove Tween solution and wash the samples with PBS.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate all remaining 0.5% TWEEN® 20 in 1X PBS from the DBS wells and discard, moving tips gently along the bottom to dislodge DBS.
Fill a sterile reservoir with 1X PBS (no Tween® 20).
Using a P1000 multichannel pipet, add 1 ml of 1X PBS to each well with DBS.
Vortex briefly and incubate at 4°C for 15-30 min.

steps.title: Prepare for Chelex Addition
steps.instruction: Remove wash buffer and prepare the plate for Chelex.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the water bath to reach 95°C (203°F).
Centrifuge the plate at 800 rpm for 1 min and aspirate as much fluid as possible.
Use the tip to press the filter paper down into the lower third of the well without packing it excessively.

steps.title: Add Chelex Solution
steps.instruction: Add the 10% Chelex solution using wide-orifice tips to avoid clogging.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a row of p200 Rainin wide-orifice tips and a sterile reservoir.
Vortex the 10% Chelex solution until it is a homogenous white cloudy liquid and pour it into the reservoir.
Using the p200 wide-orifice tips, transfer 150 µL of 10% Chelex solution into every well, depressing the liquid directly into each row to avoid cross-contamination.
If Chelex settles in the reservoir, gently move tips along the bottom and pipette up and down to re-suspend.

steps.title: DNA Extraction
steps.instruction: Incubate the samples in a heat block to extract genomic DNA.

substeps.instruction: Ensure Chelex solution and DBS are at the bottom of each well.
Seal the plate with a foil seal and centrifuge briefly at 300 rpm to collect all liquid at the bottom.
Incubate the plate for 10 min in a 95°C water bath, vigorously vortexing the plate every 2 minutes.
After incubation, centrifuge the plate at 1500 rpm for 5 minutes (ensure proper balance).

steps.title: Transfer and Clarify DNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the DNA elution to a transfer plate and pellet the beads.

substeps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipet, transfer as much solution as possible from the spun plate to a non-skirted 96-well transfer plate (for better visualization).
Move the tip along the bottom of the well to dislodge DBS and ensure all liquid is aspirated.
Seal the transfer plate and spin for 10 minutes at 1500 rpm.

steps.title: Final DNA Aliquoting
steps.instruction: Transfer the clarified DNA supernatant to the final storage plate.

substeps.instruction: Using a P20 multichannel pipet, slowly aspirate the white-to-yellowish supernatant from the middle/top of the well to avoid disturbing the Chelex beads.
Transfer a minimum of 100 µL per well to the labeled DNA Lobind Plate.
If beads are aspirated, dispense the liquid back into the transfer plate and let beads settle for a few minutes.
Ensure no tip contacts more than one sample and samples match the plate-map.

steps.title: Storage and Labeling
steps.instruction: Seal and store the final plates.

substeps.instruction: Carefully seal the final DNA plate and label as 'SamplePlateName_DNA' using the label printer.
Store the DNA plate at -20°C.
If protein plasma was saved, label the Protein plates (Lobind Protein Deepwell plates) as 'SamplePlateName_Protein'.
